text:
Memento at the San Isidro fair



Little heart, scarcely elegiac, weary of science

the sad books unread, the ambiguous prayers

embarked without a wristwatch, ignorant of the stars

weary of wisdom, the astrolabe is a nominative.



Movement too is weary and dragged out

metronomic because it is number, not name

the train crosses the bridge and then falls.



Little of a night owl, yet disoriented and afflicted

by confusion tangled in irregular actions

the verbs, the pronouns punished facing the wall.

Entirely kind.



Ash of all the ashes, enamored ash:

the priapic, gagged and dry, trembling

to make an amulet of it, tell friends about it

to leap from the top floor.

















Whistling her tune to the left

with the train beneath her peach-shaped buttocks

a tooth still piercing her breast

and her leg's disdain for the nylon stocking

on the way to airing out a love affair

she plunges into the sea and orders two horchatas

toasting the air: “Cheers, cheers!”

the burnished athlete then approaches

“I know what's happening, and your Weltanschauung—

your willfulness, I mean;

he, by contrast—plagiarizing Scott Fitzgerald—

is scholastic even when buying tobacco.”

She cries out joyfully and smiles

at night, and in intimate union the two urinate

and sing in duet:

“Nothing is as clear as the human sciences,

nothing as Taylorist as psychiatry.”
